definition: Industrial artificial intelligence, or industrial AI, refers to the application of artificial intelligence to industrial business processes.
details: Unlike general artificial intelligence which is a frontier research discipline to build computerized systems that perform tasks requiring human intelligence, industrial AI is more concerned with the application of such technologies to address industrial pain-points for customer value creation, productivity improvement, cost reduction, site optimization, predictive analysis and insight discovery. Artificial intelligence and machine learning have become key enablers to leverage data in production in recent years due to a number of different factors: More affordable sensors and the automated process of data acquisition; More powerful computation capability of computers to perform more complex tasks at a faster speed with lower cost; Faster connectivity infrastructure and more accessible cloud services for data management and computing power outsourcing.

explainer.lead: Industrial AI puts artificial intelligence to work on practical industrial problems, from reducing costs to improving productivity. The aim is useful business and operational results, rather than building machines with general human intelligence.

tiers.eli5: Industrial AI is like giving a factory a very observant helper. It looks at information collected while work is happening, finds useful patterns, and helps people make the work faster, cheaper, or better.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply industrial AI to production data and business processes, often using machine learning for predictive analysis, site optimization, and insight discovery. Affordable sensors, automated data acquisition, faster computers, connectivity, and accessible cloud services make these systems practical. A key pitfall is treating the analysis as the goal: the result still has to address an operational pain point and deliver value.
tiers.paperLevel: Industrial AI can be expressed as the application of artificial intelligence methods to industrial business processes, with objectives including customer value creation, productivity improvement, cost reduction, site optimization, predictive analysis, and insight discovery. Its scope is application-oriented, unlike general artificial intelligence, which is frontier research into systems performing tasks that require human intelligence. Its practical feasibility depends on data acquisition, computation, connectivity, and data-management infrastructure.

explainer.example: A production facility automatically gathers sensor readings and sends them to a cloud service for machine-learning analysis. The analysis reveals a useful pattern in the production data, which the operations team uses to adjust the process and reduce cost while tracking whether productivity improves.

explainer.intuition: Industrial AI turns operational data into decisions that address specific industrial pain points. Its value comes from improving a real process, not from pursuing general human-like intelligence.
howItWorks: Identify an industrial pain point, such as excessive cost or low productivity.
Collect operational data through sensors and automated data acquisition.
Use computers or cloud services to manage the data and run AI or machine-learning analysis.
Turn predictions or discovered insights into process or site improvements.
Assess whether the change improves productivity, cost, optimization, or customer value.
explainer.whyItMatters: It gives industrial organizations a practical way to make use of production data. Cheaper sensing, stronger computation, faster connectivity, and accessible cloud services have made this increasingly feasible.
misconceptions: Industrial AI is not the same as general artificial intelligence; it focuses on applying AI to industrial problems.
It is not just an algorithm: data acquisition, computing, connectivity, and data management also enable it.
Producing a prediction is not the end goal; the application must create operational or customer value.
